claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulation with optimized interatomic potentials can predict the formation of stable RHEA-Cu composite structures at the atomic scale.
Molecular dynamics simulation with optimized interatomic potentials can enable large-scale RHEA-Cu reaction.
The initial material consists of RHEAs and Cu in separate states.
The proposed intervention is molecular dynamics simulation using optimized interatomic potentials.
The proposed method is intended for high-temperature conditions potentially representative of a nuclear-reactor environment.
Optimized interatomic potentials constitute the structural mediator.
The method computationally predicts and optimizes interactions between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
The proposed method will produce stable RHEA-Cu composite structures.
The resulting RHEA-Cu composite structures will have improved mechanical strength.
The resulting RHEA-Cu composite structures will have improved irradiation resistance.
The resulting RHEA-Cu composite structures will have improved thermal stability.
Previous attempts to form RHEA-Cu composite structures were hindered by a positive heat of mixing.
The proposed simulation-time range is 10–100 ns.
The proposed simulation-temperature range is 300–1000 K.
Genetic algorithms or machine-learning approaches may be used to optimize the interatomic potentials.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism characterize molecular dynamics as a computational prediction/design method, whereas the falsification experiment refers to physical composite structures being 'formed using' molecular dynamics. Simulation alone does not physically fabricate specimens for the listed mechanical, irradiation, and thermal tests.
